headline: Impeachment Court Orders Some Prosecutors to Explain Possible Sub Judice Violation
seoTitle: Impeachment Court Issues Show-Cause Orders Over Possible Sub Judice Violation | FMB News
seoDescription: The Senate impeachment court ordered some House prosecutors in Vice President Sara Duterte's trial to explain a possible violation of its sub judice rule, according to current reporting.
deck: The order requires explanations and is not itself a finding that the prosecutors committed a violation. The underlying impeachment allegations against Vice President Sara Duterte remain contested and unresolved.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate impeachment court issued show-cause orders Wednesday to some members of the House prosecution panel in Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial over a possible violation of the court's sub judice rule, the Philippine Daily Inquirer reported.
A show-cause order requires the recipients to explain their conduct. It does not by itself establish that a violation occurred or impose guilt or liability.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The procedural development occurred during Day 26 of the impeachment proceedings, the same day retired Supreme Court justices appeared as amici curiae to discuss disputed procedural questions before the court.
The impeachment court is continuing to address procedural issues while the substantive allegations against Duterte remain contested and have not been finally adjudicated.

sections.heading: What remains unresolved
paragraphs: The prosecutors' responses and any subsequent ruling or sanction from the impeachment court remain pending. FMB News will not characterize the possible sub judice violation as established unless the court formally finds one.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The order concerns the court's control over public statements while an impeachment trial is pending. How the Senate applies its sub judice rule can affect what parties and lawyers may publicly discuss during the proceeding without resolving the merits of the impeachment case itself.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the prosecutors' formal explanations and any subsequent order from the Senate impeachment court. Separate procedural rulings on the voting threshold and other trial mechanics also remain pending.

verificationNotes: Inquirer directly reports the issuance of show-cause orders to some House prosecutors for a possible sub judice violation.
GMA's live coverage independently establishes the ongoing Day 26 impeachment proceedings and procedural context.
The article explicitly distinguishes a show-cause order from a finding of violation.
The underlying impeachment allegations remain contested and are not stated as proven facts.
